key_insight: Rotor-slipstream treatment near the kite wing reverses the predicted lift effect, from a 1.9% increase for an undeformed tube to a 3.5% decrease for a wing-deflected slipstream.
engineering_relevance: Wake-resolved modeling helps assess crosswind-kite performance and downstream farm losses, including a predicted 2.2% aerodynamic-power reduction one loop diameter downstream.
method: Vortex step aerodynamics coupled to a time-marching free vortex wake in OpenFAWE.
Lumped-mass tether and actuator-disc rotors releasing vortex rings.
Single- and multiple-kite simulations with wake-length and vortex-core checks.
evidence_signal: Validation matched an independent vortex step code to 10^-9 for the M600 and within 0.3% in lift and 0.9% in drag for the V3 kite; V3 lift agreed with RANS within 3.1%.
watch_item: Free rotor-ring simulations did not converge with time-step refinement, making rotor–wing interaction predictions sensitive to slipstream modeling.
paper_title: Free-vortex-wake dynamics of airborne wind energy kites in crosswind flight
